subject.title: [Security] Host header injection vulnerability in control plane HTTP server

question: Does current main expose any authenticated or unauthenticated Gateway HTTP path that derives an externally consumed absolute URL from Host or forwarded-host request data, and what existing trusted-origin contract should govern it?
rationale: The reported source locations and impacts are not yet tied to a concrete current-main request path; choosing an allowlist or a new configured origin without that trace could create an incompatible or incomplete security change.

options.title: Perform focused security validation
options.body: Trace absolute URL, redirect, OAuth callback, and reset-link construction from Gateway HTTP entry points and patch only a confirmed attacker-controlled host flow.

options.title: Request a concrete reproduction
options.body: Ask the reporter to provide the endpoint, request headers, and resulting Location or generated URL if maintainers cannot reproduce a relevant construction path quickly.

recommendation.title: Perform focused security validation
recommendation.body: Trace absolute URL, redirect, OAuth callback, and reset-link construction from Gateway HTTP entry points and patch only a confirmed attacker-controlled host flow.

likelyOwner.reason: No feature-history owner could be established safely from the available evidence.
